slides.title: 7 signs Mom or Dad may need more help at home
slides.lead: Small changes are often the first clue.

slides.title: Unopened mail and unpaid bills
slides.text: Piles on the table, late notices, or the same bill paid twice.

slides.title: Pills left over, or running out early
slides.text: Count what is left in the bottles against what should be left.

slides.title: An empty or out-of-date fridge
slides.text: Skipped meals and spoiled food can mean cooking has become hard.

slides.title: New dents on the car
slides.text: Scrapes and dents can be an early sign that driving is getting harder.

slides.title: Missed appointments
slides.text: Forgotten visits, or not remembering what the doctor said.

slides.title: A home that looks different
slides.text: Clutter, laundry piling up, the same clothes day after day.

slides.title: Bruises or stories of falls
slides.text: Even a small fall is worth mentioning to their doctor.

slides.title: Noticed one or two?
slides.text: Start a gentle conversation, write down what you see, and talk to their doctor.

posts.caption:
Many families only notice these when they visit after a long gap, like at Thanksgiving.

None of them means something is wrong on its own. Together, they are a sign to start a gentle conversation and talk to the doctor.

Save this and share it with your brothers and sisters.

slides.title: The first 7 days after a parent's hospital stay
slides.lead: What to do, day by day, when Mom or Dad comes home.

slides.title: Understand the discharge papers
slides.text: Before you leave, ask the nurse to walk you through them. Write down who to call with questions.

slides.title: Pick up new prescriptions
slides.text: On the way home, so there is no gap the first night.

slides.title: Update the medicine list
slides.text: Compare the old list with the new one. Put away anything the doctor stopped.

slides.title: Book the follow-up visit
slides.text: The discharge papers say when. Add it to the family calendar.

slides.title: Make the home safer
slides.text: Clear the paths, add night lights, and keep the phone within reach.

slides.title: Share the visits
slides.text: Agree who checks in each day, so nobody does it all alone.

slides.title: Check how it's going
slides.text: Eating, sleeping, moving? Look again at the warning signs on the papers, and call the doctor if anything worries you.
